coarse_request: Please design a comprehensive IT and web project workflow that includes the roles of 'IT department', 'management', 'web design team', '3PASWG', and 'ISTG'. The key activities are 'hardware procurement', 'data validation', 'web design', and 'B2B U-Turn implementation', and there should be decision points regarding 'request approval', 'site approval', and 'security review'.
fine_grained_text:
Step 1: The process of buying new hardware is started as soon as a request for new hardware is received by the IT department.
The next step is for the IT department to analyse the request and either approve or deny it.
If it is denied, the employee is informed via email about the denial and the process is ended.
However, if the request is approved it is edited and completed.
Then an email is sent to the supplier asking about prices.
Then the supplier replies to the email by sending an offer for the requested items.
Once this offer is received, a form is filled in and sent to the management.
The management then analyses the request and decides if it is approved or not.
In the former case, the offer is forwarded to the financial department and back to the IT department.
The financial department finds resources while the IT department prepares an order and sends this to the supplier.
When this is accepted and the financial resources are found the hardware is received by the IT department.
After which the financial department will take care of the invoice and the processes is ended.
In the scenario where the management does not approve the request it can send the request back to the IT department for rework, then the IT department has to go back to editing and completing a request.
If the management does not approve the request it can also decide to deny the request after which the process is ended.
[Transition]: Following the hardware procurement process, if a data validation error occurs during the financial invoice processing or system recording of the new hardware, the IS system notifies the appropriate personnel, initiating the data validation error resolution process.
Step 2: The process starts when the IS is notified about a data validation error.
The drop-off tech checks for typos.
If this is not the case, the technician checks if the customer can correct the mistake.
Otherwise, public sources are scoured for solutions.
As soon as any check was passed, the issue is considered resolved.
[Transition]: After the data validation issue is resolved, the web design team holds an informational meeting to plan the next phase of the web project.
Step 3: The process starts with an informational meeting among the web design team.
If this meeting is not successful, the process ends here.
Otherwise, the team starts by creating a storyboard.
After an agreement on the storyboard, part of the team starts working on the design and development of the website.
Simultaneously, the team will start to prepare an initial draft of the content.
In case a review of the draft is needed, the marketing team will conduct this, before the web design team creates the final version of the content.
When the development and content have been completed, the website will be built and reviewed.
If the site is approved, the process is completed, otherwise the team goes back to the building step.
[Transition]: Following the successful completion of the web design and development process, the approved website often requires supporting IT infrastructure and tools, which initiates Process B when departments submit IT solution requests to implement the necessary software and hardware systems.
Step 4: The process starts when an employee or department submits a request for an IT solution, such as new software or hardware.
IT assesses the request, checking for compatibility with existing systems and evaluating cost and resource needs.
If approved, IT procures the necessary tools or licenses, installs the solution, and tests it in a controlled environment.
After successful testing, the new solution is rolled out to the requesting department.
Training may be provided, and IT support remains available for troubleshooting.
[Transition]: Upon completion of the standard IT implementation and training phase, if the solution requires inter-corporation business-to-business network connectivity or U-turn implementation, the Citigroup B2B U-Turn Request workflow is activated to address the specialized security and technical requirements for external network connections.
Step 5: The Citigroup Inter-Corporation Business-to-Business (B2B) Network U-Turn Request workflow is as follows:
1. Requestors submit a NE Project Request for B2B U-Turn implementation.
2. The 3rd Party Access Solutions Workgroup (3PASWG) receives product order requests, analyzes requirements, and then assigns a network engineer.
3. 3PASWG notifies the requestor of B2B U-Turn implementation requirements and the CCR approval process. The requestor obtained business justification, a BISO statement of compliance, and a signed B2B U-Turn notification letter in the notification. At the same time, 3PASWG creates a high-level B2B U-Turn diagram for providing it to the requestor.
4. Requestors submit B2B U-Turn approval requests in CCR. The 3PASWG then reviews the request, and immediately thereafter, it refers the request to the Information Security Technology Group (ISTG) for review.
5. ISTG reviews the request and notifies the requester of rejection or approval, depending on its review. The process ends after rejection. If the review notifies the requestor of approval, the requestor receives an approval notification and notifies NE. After the requester is notified of the approval, the 3PASWG first proceeds with the design and implementation of the B2B U-Turn and then advises the requester to register the U-Turn in the CCR. The process ends when the requester registers a B2B U-Turn in CCR.
